title: Built Here, Owned Elsewhere: Who Owns the Black Consumer Market | At The Margins, Ep. 1
lede: Black consumers in the U.S. command about $2 trillion in buying power. Black-owned companies with employees are 3.4% of U.S. employer firms, and Black brands took 2.5% of U.S. beauty revenue in 2021. Episode 1 of At The Margins follows the money from the checkout line to the balance sheet, in the U.S. and Canada, and traces how four of the best-known Black-founded beauty brands were sold to L'Oréal, Unilever and P&G.
keyPoints: Black-owned employer firms: 201,000 in 2023 (the latest Census year), 3.4% of all, with $249.0B in receipts and 1.8M+ jobs; up 62% since 2017 vs 3.3% for all firms (Census; Brookings).
On Oct 22, 2026, the Census Bureau proposed dropping owner race and other demographic questions from the next Annual Business Survey; comments close Dec 21 (Federal Register).

In Canada, Black-owned enterprises were 2.8% of the total in 2022 vs a 4.3% population share (Statistics Canada); FACE's Black Entrepreneurship Loan Fund has disbursed $50.4M to nearly 600 businesses.
Black consumers made 11.1% of U.S. beauty spending in 2021; Black brands took 2.5% of revenue, and 9 of 45 Black beauty brands no longer Black-owned held 82% of the group's revenue (McKinsey).
Carol's Daughter, Sundial, Walker & Co. and Mielle were sold to L'Oréal, Unilever and P&G; Essence (2018) and Carol's Daughter (2025) show ownership bought back.
